description: Compact independent static checks for selected Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Dockerfile, container YAML, Terraform and dependency declaration mechanisms. No Analyzer parity or runtime verification claim.

rules.title: Dynamic Python code execution
rules.criteria: Recognize eval/exec calls; ast.literal_eval is the narrow data-only alternative.
rules.next_action: Keep input as data; use a fixed operation or a data-only parser.

rules.title: Python subprocess uses a shell
rules.criteria: Recognize literal shell=True and interfaces that always use a shell: os.system, os.popen, subprocess.getoutput/getstatusoutput and asyncio.create_subprocess_shell. A literal argument list without a shell satisfies this specific check.
rules.next_action: Use a fixed executable and an argument list with shell=False; validate operation-specific arguments.

rules.title: SQL execution receives a constructed expression
rules.criteria: Recognize f-strings and binary expressions passed to execute/executemany; literal SQL satisfies only this construction check.
rules.next_action: Use a constant query with database-bound parameters.

rules.title: Python certificate verification disabled
rules.criteria: Recognize requests and httpx calls or clients with verify=False, ssl._create_unverified_context(), and SSL context assignments of check_hostname=False or verify_mode=ssl.CERT_NONE. Verification enabled explicitly or by the documented default satisfies this check.
rules.next_action: Keep certificate verification enabled and configure the appropriate trust store.

rules.title: YAML executable object loader selected
rules.criteria: Recognize yaml.load/load_all with Loader/UnsafeLoader or their C variants and yaml.unsafe_load/unsafe_load_all; recognize safe_load, safe_load_all and SafeLoader.
rules.next_action: Use yaml.safe_load or an explicitly safe data-only loader.

rules.title: Pickle deserialization requires a trusted source
rules.criteria: Recognize pickle.load/loads. Whether the input is attacker-controlled requires separate verification.
rules.next_action: Avoid pickle across trust boundaries; parse an appropriate data-only format.

rules.title: MD5 or SHA-1 with a named security purpose
rules.criteria: Recognize hashlib.md5/sha1 on a line naming signature, token, password, credential, secret or HMAC. Other hash calls do not prove an adequate security mechanism.
rules.next_action: Select a suitable established mechanism for the purpose; use a password KDF for passwords.

rules.title: Flask-style debug flag enabled
rules.criteria: Recognize app.run(debug=True/False); deployment exposure is not established.
rules.next_action: Keep the debug server isolated from untrusted recipients and disable debug for deployed service operation.

rules.title: Predictable Python random value for a named secret
rules.criteria: Recognize random module calls on a line whose identifiers name a token, secret, OTP, nonce, salt, CSRF value, password, session ID, API key or private key. secrets, os.urandom and random.SystemRandom satisfy this check.
rules.next_action: Generate secret values with the secrets module.

rules.title: Python token verification disabled or unrestricted
rules.criteria: Recognize jwt.decode calls. verify=False, options disabling verify_signature or verify_exp, and an allowed 'none' algorithm violate this check. A literal algorithm list, including module-level string constants, satisfies it; other algorithm or option values remain unclear.
rules.next_action: Verify signatures and expiry and pass an explicit list of the expected algorithms.

rules.title: JavaScript code evaluation
rules.criteria: Recognize eval/Function calls outside comments, string and regular-expression literals; JSON.parse is a data-only alternative. Selector helpers such as $eval are not evaluation.
rules.next_action: Use fixed application operations and keep input as data.

examples.source: const label = await page.$eval('#title', node => node.textContent);

rules.title: JavaScript command execution through exec
rules.criteria: Recognize exec/execSync calls with a narrow child_process import binding. Unresolved bare or member calls remain unclear; unrelated object.exec methods do not produce shell findings.
rules.next_action: Use an explicitly selected executable with an argument array and review shell options.

rules.title: Predictable random value for a named secret
rules.criteria: Recognize Math.random on a line whose identifiers name a token, secret, OTP, nonce, salt, CSRF value, password, session ID, API key or private key, matched by camelCase and snake_case segments; recognize crypto random APIs.
rules.next_action: Generate security values with a cryptographic random API.

rules.title: Node MD5 or SHA-1 with a named security purpose
rules.criteria: Recognize createHash('md5'|'sha1') on a line whose identifiers name a signature, token, password, credential, secret or HMAC. Other algorithms with such a purpose remain unclear; they do not prove an adequate mechanism.
rules.next_action: Select a suitable established mechanism for the purpose; use a password KDF for passwords.

rules.title: Assignment to an HTML interpretation sink
rules.criteria: Recognize innerHTML/outerHTML assignment including +=, insertAdjacentHTML and document.write/writeln; the narrow safe text alternative is textContent. Sanitizers and element context need separate verification.
rules.next_action: Prefer textContent; if HTML is required, verify appropriate sanitization at the actual sink.

rules.title: Node certificate verification disabled
rules.criteria: Recognize literal rejectUnauthorized:false/true and NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED assignments of '0'/'1' in code outside comments and strings.
rules.next_action: Keep certificate verification enabled and configure trusted certificates.

rules.title: JavaScript token verification allows none or ignores expiry
rules.criteria: Inspect literal options of jwt.verify/jsonwebtoken.verify and express-jwt calls, including ESM/require aliases. An allowed 'none' algorithm or ignoreExpiration: true violates this check; an explicit literal algorithm list with no unresolved expiry override satisfies it. Missing, dynamic, spread or duplicate relevant options remain unclear. Unrelated algorithms fields and decode-only calls are not assessed.
rules.next_action: Verify tokens with an explicit list of expected signing algorithms and keep expiry checks enabled.

examples.source:
import { verify as check } from 'jsonwebtoken';
check(token, key, { ignoreExpiration: true });

import { expressjwt as guard } from 'express-jwt';
guard({ secret: key, algorithms: ['RS256'] });

rules.title: Remote GitHub Action uses a mutable reference
rules.criteria: Recognize remote uses declarations; a complete 40-hex commit or Docker digest satisfies the pinning check. A pin is not a vulnerability assessment.
rules.next_action: Pin third-party actions to reviewed immutable commits or container digests.

rules.title: Container base image has no immutable digest
rules.criteria: Recognize FROM references in Dockerfile and Containerfile variants; inspect all stages independently. A reference to an earlier stage alias pulls no image and is skipped. Variables need context.
rules.next_action: Pin external base images to reviewed immutable digests.

examples.source:
FROM node@sha256:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa AS build
FROM build AS runtime

rules.title: Final container stage selects a non-root user
rules.criteria: Positive evidence only. The last USER of the final stage is a literal non-root identity. Root, a variable or a missing USER is no evidence either way, because the base image or the platform can set the runtime user.
rules.next_action: Keep a non-root identity for the runtime stage.

examples.source:
FROM builder
USER app
FROM example
USER root

FROM builder
USER app
FROM example

rules.title: Container build pipes a download to an interpreter
rules.criteria: Inspect RUN instructions, joined across line continuations, for curl/wget piped to a shell (also through sudo or sh -c "$(curl ...)") and Invoke-WebRequest piped to Invoke-Expression. Other downloads remain unverified.
rules.next_action: Download to a file, verify a pinned checksum or signature, then execute it.

examples.source:
RUN apt-get update \
  && curl -fsSL https://example.invalid/install.sh | bash

rules.title: Container build adds a remote source without a pin
rules.criteria: Recognize ADD with an HTTP(S) source. --checksum=sha256 or a Git source pinned to a full commit satisfies this check.
rules.next_action: Pin remote build inputs with --checksum or a full commit, or copy reviewed local files.

rules.title: Container receives host-level privileges
rules.criteria: Inspect YAML keys: privileged, allowPrivilegeEscalation, hostNetwork, hostPID and hostIPC set to true, Compose network_mode/pid/ipc host, and a mounted Docker socket violate this check. Explicit false values satisfy it; templated values remain unclear. Whether the file is deployed is not established.
rules.next_action: Remove host-level privileges; grant only the specific capabilities and mounts the workload needs.

rules.title: Constructed SQL passed to a query call
rules.criteria: Recognize query/execute, $queryRawUnsafe and $executeRawUnsafe calls starting with literal SQL. Interpolation and concatenation are violations; literal SQL satisfies only this construction check. Variable queries remain unclear.
rules.next_action: Use a literal SQL statement and driver-bound parameters.

rules.title: Frontend bypasses protected output handling
rules.criteria: Recognize React dangerouslySetInnerHTML and Angular bypassSecurityTrust APIs. Intrinsic JSX text children and Angular component interpolation are narrow positive signals, not framework-wide protection.
rules.next_action: Prefer framework text binding; verify sanitization at any deliberate HTML or trust bypass.

rules.title: CSP declares unsafe script execution
rules.criteria: Recognize literal enforced CSP declarations. Wildcard, unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval, data: and broad HTTP(S) script sources violate this check, except where browsers ignore them: unsafe-inline next to a nonce or hash, and host and scheme sources next to strict-dynamic. Positive declarations restrict scripts and set object-src none, base-uri none and frame-ancestors. Delivery and nonce generation remain unverified.
rules.next_action: Review the delivered policy and remove unsafe script execution allowances.

rules.title: Browser security header declaration
rules.criteria: Positive evidence only. Recognize literal X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY or SAMEORIGIN, Strict-Transport-Security with a positive max-age and a restrictive Referrer-Policy, and helmet() or its header middlewares for an imported helmet binding. helmet() counts all four headers unless an option names one; middleware options are not evaluated. A missing, weak or dynamic value is no evidence either way, because a proxy or platform outside the repository may set the header. Delivery on every response remains unverified.
rules.next_action: Verify that the headers are delivered on every response, including through proxies.

rules.title: Dependency uses an insecure or mutable Git source
rules.criteria: Inspect npm declarations. HTTP sources and Git dependencies without a full commit violate this check. Registry resolution requires lock evidence; local/workspace sources remain unclear.
rules.next_action: Use TLS and reviewed immutable commits for Git dependencies; maintain a consistent lockfile.

rules.title: Install lifecycle pipes a download to an interpreter
rules.criteria: Inspect preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare scripts for curl/wget piped to a shell (also through sudo or sh -c "$(curl ...)") or Invoke-WebRequest piped to Invoke-Expression. Other scripts remain unverified.
rules.next_action: Remove download-and-execute hooks; use reviewed pinned artifacts with integrity verification.

rules.title: Dependency lock evidence is unavailable or inconsistent
rules.criteria: A selected npm v2/v3 lock whose root dependency declarations match package.json is a positive consistency signal. Missing, stale, other-manager or out-of-scope locks remain unclear. This does not establish package integrity or vulnerability status.
rules.next_action: Maintain a reviewed lockfile and use frozen install mode.

rules.title: Python install requirements are not exactly pinned
rules.criteria: Inspect active requirement lines joined across backslash continuations. Floating requirements, HTTP sources, --extra-index-url, --trusted-host and editable VCS sources without a full commit violate this check. An exact version is a positive declaration; a SHA-256 hash also binds the downloaded file. Includes, other options and local paths remain unclear.
rules.next_action: Use reviewed exact versions and hashes for reproducible application installation; inspect included constraints and package indexes.

rules.title: Workflow requests write-all permissions
rules.criteria: Recognize explicit write-all and read-all GitHub workflow permissions. Scoped or inherited permissions need context; absence is not proof of missing protection.
rules.next_action: Grant only the permissions required by each job.

rules.title: Workflow expands untrusted event text into a script
rules.criteria: Inspect run and github-script script values, including block scalars, for ${{ }} expressions that read attacker-editable event fields: issue, pull request and discussion titles and bodies, comment and review bodies, head refs and labels, commit messages and author names. Values passed through env are not expanded into the script and do not match.
rules.next_action: Pass the value through an environment variable and quote it in the script instead of expanding it with ${{ }}.

examples.source:
on: issues
jobs:
  triage:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: |
          echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"

on: issues
jobs:
  triage:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "$TITLE"
        env:
          TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}

rules.title: Privileged pull request workflow checks out proposed code
rules.criteria: In workflows triggered by pull_request_target or workflow_run, recognize ref values that select the pull request head, head branch or merge ref, and gh pr checkout. These triggers run with repository secrets and write tokens; whether the checked-out code is executed is not established.
rules.next_action: Run untrusted pull request code in a pull_request workflow without secrets, or keep the privileged workflow from checking out or executing it.

examples.source:
on: pull_request_target
jobs:
  preview:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

on: pull_request
jobs:
  preview:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

rules.title: Repository host control is not enabled: default_branch_protection
rules.criteria: Only explicit true/enabled API state satisfies this check; explicit false/disabled violates it. Inaccessible or omitted fields remain unclear.
rules.next_action: Review the contribution and release policy and configure the applicable host control.

rules.title: Repository host control is not enabled: required_reviews
rules.criteria: Only explicit true/enabled API state satisfies this check; explicit false/disabled violates it. Inaccessible or omitted fields remain unclear.
rules.next_action: Review the contribution and release policy and configure the applicable host control.

rules.title: Repository host control is not enabled: secret_scanning
rules.criteria: Only explicit true/enabled API state satisfies this check; explicit false/disabled violates it. Inaccessible or omitted fields remain unclear.
rules.next_action: Review the contribution and release policy and configure the applicable host control.

rules.title: Repository host control is not enabled: dependabot_security_updates
rules.criteria: Only explicit true/enabled API state satisfies this check; explicit false/disabled violates it. Inaccessible or omitted fields remain unclear.
rules.next_action: Review the contribution and release policy and configure the applicable host control.

rules.title: Repository host control is not enabled: successful_pipeline_before_merge
rules.criteria: Only explicit true/enabled API state satisfies this check; explicit false/disabled violates it. Inaccessible or omitted fields remain unclear.
rules.next_action: Review the contribution and release policy and configure the applicable host control.

rules.title: Repository host control is not enabled: security_scanning
rules.criteria: Only explicit true/enabled API state satisfies this check; explicit false/disabled violates it. Inaccessible or omitted fields remain unclear.
rules.next_action: Review the contribution and release policy and configure the applicable host control.

rules.title: Repository host requires signed commits
rules.criteria: Positive evidence only. A ruleset rule requires signatures on the default branch. Its absence is no evidence either way, because classic protection is not readable without admin rights.
rules.next_action: Keep signature requirements for the default branch.

rules.title: Credential or key file in the repository
rules.criteria: Recognize environment, credential and private key file names from the file list. These files stay excluded from reading, so whether one holds a live secret is not established. Example environment files and certificate-named PEM files do not match.
rules.next_action: Remove the file from the repository, rotate anything it exposed, and load the value from a secret store.

rules.title: Credential in a recognized format
rules.criteria: Recognize prefixed AWS, GitHub, GitLab, Slack, npm, Stripe and Anthropic credentials and PEM private keys with key material. Generic high-entropy strings, documentation samples and repeated placeholder characters do not match. Whether a credential is live is not established, and output never contains its value.
rules.next_action: Revoke the credential, remove it from the history, and load the value from a secret store.

examples.source: const key = '-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\r\nMIIEpAIBAAKCAQEA0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEF\r\n-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----';

rules.title: CI step pipes a download to an interpreter
rules.criteria: Inspect GitHub workflow run values and GitLab script, before_script and after_script values for curl/wget piped to a shell (also through sudo or sh -c "$(curl ...)") and Invoke-WebRequest piped to Invoke-Expression. Other downloads remain unverified.
rules.next_action: Download to a file, verify a pinned checksum or signature, then execute it.

examples.source:
jobs:
  build:
    steps:
      - run: curl -sSL https://example.invalid/install.sh | bash

jobs:
  build:
    steps:
      - run: |
          # curl https://example.invalid/install.sh | bash
          curl -o install.sh https://example.invalid/install.sh

rules.title: Build installs npm packages without the lockfile mode
rules.criteria: In CI scripts and Dockerfile RUN instructions, npm install without named packages can change the lockfile. npm ci and yarn or pnpm with a frozen or immutable flag satisfy this check. Named packages and global tools are other operations.
rules.next_action: Use npm ci so a build installs exactly the reviewed lockfile.

examples.source:
jobs:
  build:
    steps:
      - run: npm install

FROM example
RUN npm install -g example-tool

rules.title: GitLab CI image has no immutable digest
rules.criteria: Recognize image values in GitLab CI files, including the name form. A sha256 digest satisfies this check. Values with variables usually name the project's own registry and are not assessed.
rules.next_action: Pin external CI images to reviewed immutable digests.

rules.title: GitLab CI include uses a mutable reference
rules.criteria: Remote, project and component includes run code from outside this repository. A full commit in the URL, ref or component version satisfies this check. Local and template includes are not assessed, and a variable ref stays unresolved.
rules.next_action: Pin included CI configuration to a reviewed full commit.

examples.source:
include:
  - project: group/ci
    ref: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
    file: /ci.yml

rules.title: GitLab CI evaluates contributor-controlled text
rules.criteria: Inspect GitLab script values for eval or sh -c combined with contributor-editable variables such as commit messages, merge request titles and source branch names. The shell only expands these variables, so a plain echo does not match.
rules.next_action: Pass the value as data and never evaluate it as a command.

rules.title: Lockfile entry from an unusual source or without integrity
rules.criteria: Inspect package-lock.json and npm-shrinkwrap.json resolved URLs. HTTP, a host beside the public registries and the file's most frequent host, and an entry without integrity violate this check. This does not establish package safety or vulnerability status.
rules.next_action: Review the entry, restore it from the registry, and regenerate the lockfile.

rules.title: Dependency source is unencrypted or mutable
rules.criteria: In pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, pom.xml and Gradle build files, HTTP repositories, allowInsecureProtocol, extra index URLs and Git dependencies without a full commit violate this check. HTTPS repositories and Git dependencies with a full commit satisfy it. Other manifests are not assessed.
rules.next_action: Use HTTPS repositories and pin Git dependencies to a reviewed full commit.

rules.title: Compiled binary in the repository
rules.criteria: Recognize compiled artifacts from the file list. Reviewers cannot read them, and generated directories such as dist and target are skipped. The Gradle wrapper is excluded because it has its own validation.
rules.next_action: Build the artifact from source or fetch a pinned release instead of committing it.

rules.title: Security policy file
rules.criteria: Positive evidence only. A missing file is no evidence either way, because an organization can publish its policy centrally.
rules.next_action: Keep the reporting contact in the policy current.

rules.title: Dependency update configuration
rules.criteria: Positive evidence only. A missing file is no evidence either way, because updates can be configured centrally. A configuration does not show that updates are merged.
rules.next_action: Review and merge the proposed updates regularly.

rules.title: Dependency manifest has no lockfile
rules.criteria: A package.json with dependencies, a Pipfile, and a pyproject.toml with dependencies but no build backend need a lockfile of their ecosystem beside them or in a directory above, which covers workspaces. The file list decides; lockfile content is not read. A pyproject.toml with a build backend may be a library and stays unassessed. A present lockfile earns no credit, and tests, fixtures and vendored copies are skipped.
rules.next_action: Commit the lockfile and install from it, for example with npm ci or uv sync --locked.

rules.title: Release integrity step
rules.criteria: Positive evidence only. Recognize SBOM generation, cosign signing, build provenance and PyPI trusted publishing in CI files. A declared step does not show that a release used it, and a missing step is no evidence either way.
rules.next_action: Verify that published artifacts carry the declared signature or provenance.

examples.source:
permissions:
  id-token: write
jobs:
  release:
    steps:
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa

jobs:
  release:
    steps:
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
        with:
          password: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}

rules.title: Cloud login through OIDC
rules.criteria: Positive evidence only. Recognize AWS role-to-assume, Azure login with a tenant ID, GCP workload identity and GitLab id_tokens in CI files. Stored keys appear in the architecture profile as context, because a declaration does not show how a key is scoped or rotated.
rules.next_action: Keep the cloud role scoped to the branch and environment that need it.

examples.source:
jobs:
  deploy:
    steps:
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/example

jobs:
  deploy:
    steps:
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
        with:
          aws-access-key-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_KEY }}

rules.title: Container hardening setting
rules.criteria: Positive evidence only. Recognize runAsNonRoot and readOnlyRootFilesystem set to true in YAML. A missing setting is no evidence either way, and whether the file is deployed is not established.
rules.next_action: Keep the setting on every deployed workload.

rules.title: Password reaches a fast general-purpose hash
rules.criteria: Follow password-named inputs into hash calls and simple local helpers. JavaScript/TypeScript also resolves one relative ESM/require import hop to named ESM exports in already-selected complete files, without executing code. MD5, SHA-1, SHA-2 and SHA-3 violate this check; bcrypt, Argon2, scrypt, PBKDF2 and framework password hashers satisfy it without verifying their parameters. Unresolved helpers, ambiguous paths and other hashes are not assessed.
rules.next_action: Hash passwords with Argon2 or bcrypt and migrate stored values at the next login.

rules.title: Cookie disables httpOnly or secure
rules.criteria: Recognize literal httpOnly and secure flags in res.cookie, cookies.set and cookie option objects. False violates this check and true satisfies it; computed values and missing flags are not assessed.
rules.next_action: Set httpOnly and secure on session cookies.

examples.source: app.use(session({ cookie: { httpOnly: true, secure: true } }));

rules.title: Credentialed CORS accepts any origin
rules.criteria: Inspect cors() options with credentials true. A wildcard or a reflected origin violates this check, literal HTTPS origins satisfy it, and computed origins are not assessed.
rules.next_action: Allow only an exact list of trusted origins for credentialed requests.

rules.title: Django or Flask setting weakens sessions or host checks
rules.criteria: Recognize literal session and CSRF cookie settings, ALLOWED_HOSTS, and CORS_ALLOW_ALL_ORIGINS with CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS. Computed values are not assessed, and whether a settings file is used in production is not established.
rules.next_action: Enable secure session cookies and list the expected hosts and origins.

rules.title: Terraform state file in the repository
rules.criteria: Recognize state files from the file list. Terraform stores resource attributes in state, including generated passwords and keys in plain text. The content is not read.
rules.next_action: Move state to an encrypted remote backend and rotate the values it exposed.

rules.title: Administrative port open to the internet
rules.criteria: In AWS, Azure and GCP firewall declarations, an open source range with a port range covering SSH or RDP, or all protocols, violates this check. Other ports, egress, deny rules and computed values are not assessed. Whether the resource is deployed is not established.
rules.next_action: Restrict the source to a VPN or bastion range, or use a managed session service.

rules.title: Storage or database declared as public
rules.criteria: A public-read ACL, publicly_accessible true and public_network_access_enabled true violate this check. Their false values and block_public_acls or block_public_policy true satisfy it. Whether the resource is deployed is not established.
rules.next_action: Keep the resource private and expose it through an authenticated service.

rules.title: IAM statement allows every action on every resource
rules.criteria: A statement with a wildcard action and a wildcard resource violates this check, in HCL or JSON form. Deny statements and narrower statements are not assessed.
rules.next_action: List the actions and resources the role needs.

rules.title: Terraform module has no fixed version
rules.criteria: A Git or URL source without a ref or on a default branch, and a registry module without a version, violate this check. A full commit or an exact version satisfies it. Tags and version ranges are not assessed, and local modules do not apply.
rules.next_action: Pin external modules to a reviewed commit or exact version.

rules.title: Terraform dependency lock file
rules.criteria: Positive evidence only. The lock file pins provider versions and hashes. A missing file is no evidence either way.
rules.next_action: Keep the lock file reviewed and committed.

path_rules.reason: Agent instructions or prompts changed; review action authority and trusted context.
Dependency declarations, resolution or package sources changed; review supply-chain consequences.
Build, release, ownership or deployment configuration changed; review execution and privileges.
Credential or secret configuration changed; excluded contents are not read or disclosed.
Security policy or threat-model assumptions changed; review their applicability.
An access-control implementation or policy file changed; inspect the affected access decisions.
Routing, proxy or network-exposure configuration changed; inspect which interfaces and operations become reachable.

code_rules.reason: Changed code or its containing function references identity, permissions or ownership checks; inspect who may access which resource.
Changed code or its containing function declares a route or middleware; inspect interface reachability, allowed operations and access controls.
Changed code or its containing function indicates an external data flow; inspect destinations, transmitted data and credentials.
Changed code or its containing function indicates data access; inspect parameter binding, ownership and database privileges.
Changed code or its containing function indicates a security control; inspect its configuration and enforcement.
Changed code or its containing function indicates secret handling or cryptography; inspect its purpose and lifecycle.
Changed code or its containing function indicates input or output processing; inspect validation and rendering context.
Listener, binding or public-exposure configuration is in the changed context; inspect which callers can reach the interface.

execution.reason: A recognized security operation or control is in the affected change context; inspect its behavior even when no weakness is detected.

injection.reason: A recognized security operation or control is in the affected change context; inspect its behavior even when no weakness is detected.

transport.reason: A recognized security operation or control is in the affected change context; inspect its behavior even when no weakness is detected.

cryptography.reason: A recognized security operation or control is in the affected change context; inspect its behavior even when no weakness is detected.

deserialization.reason: A recognized security operation or control is in the affected change context; inspect its behavior even when no weakness is detected.

hardening.reason: A recognized security operation or control is in the affected change context; inspect its behavior even when no weakness is detected.

frontend-policy.reason: A recognized security operation or control is in the affected change context; inspect its behavior even when no weakness is detected.

supply-chain.reason: A recognized security operation or control is in the affected change context; inspect its behavior even when no weakness is detected.

output.reason: A recognized security operation or control is in the affected change context; inspect its behavior even when no weakness is detected.

authentication.reason: A recognized security operation or control is in the affected change context; inspect its behavior even when no weakness is detected.

secrets.reason: A recognized security operation or control is in the affected change context; inspect its behavior even when no weakness is detected.

infrastructure.reason: A recognized security operation or control is in the affected change context; inspect its behavior even when no weakness is detected.

documentation_rule.reason: Changed documentation contains security or installation guidance; review the described assumptions.

executable_rule.reason: Executable permission changed; review how this file can be invoked.

examples.after: cursor.execute("SELECT name FROM items WHERE id=?", (identifier,))
